1) moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoeas (OSAs) are associated with an increased incidence of nonfatal vascular events (CVEs) in stroke patients; and 2) CPAP reduces the increased incidence of CVEs in stroke patients with moderate-to severe OSAs.

the presence of severe OSA is associated, after stroke, with an increased long‐term incidence of nonfatal cardiac events and that CPAP treatment reduces the excess of events seen in stroke patients with severe OSA.

the presence of obstructive sleep apnoeas (OSAs) in patients with a recent stroke is associated with a higher incidence of cardiovascular events and that the use of continuous positive airway pressures reduces this excess.

a new and important aspect of stroke management, namely, the role of CPAP treatment in the secondary prevention of nonfatal CVE.
the long-term effects of OSA and CPAP treatment on CVE in stroke patients.
the incidence of cardiovascular events in stroke and OSA.
